topic: Experiments, sampling and the binomial distribution
title: Dice, coins and the binomial distribution
instructions:
## Simulate, then calculate

The **Sampler** rolls dice and flips coins thousands of times and compares the observed frequencies with theory. The **Statistics** tool describes a data set.

## Do this

1. Roll two dice 10,000 times. Estimate the probability that the sum is 7, then compute the exact value as a fraction.
2. Flip 5 coins. What is the probability of exactly 2 heads? Compute it from the binomial formula.
3. A trial succeeds with probability 0.3. In 5 trials, what is P(exactly 2 successes)? Compare with the sampler.
4. The data set loaded in Statistics is the number of tro-tro trips a mate made on ten days. Give the mean and the median.
hints: Six of the 36 equally likely outcomes give a sum of 7.
P(k heads in n flips) = C(n, k) / 2ⁿ; C(5, 2) = 10.
P(X = k) = C(n, k) pᵏ (1 − p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ.

realityNote: Simulation (Monte Carlo) is how engineers estimate probabilities that have no closed form, from network outages to insurance risk; the exact binomial formula is the special case you can check it against.
